summary: SDD ran all four tasks on the existing feature/textstats branch. Each task had an implementer, then a reviewer that finished before the next task was dispatched. A final Opus whole-branch review followed, and the session ended in finishing-a-development-branch. The context was auto-compacted many times. After compacting, the controller said it was re-reading SKILL.md and the ledger, then carried on with the loop. On disk: 4 feature commits, all 4 functions exported, and npm test passes 70/70.
reasoning: All four criteria are backed by the git state, a live npm test run, and dispatch timestamps from the session log. Repeated compactions did not break the task loop: implement → review was strictly sequential, a final review happened, and the session ended in the finishing skill. The branch was not created by the agent: it already existed in the fixture (reflog shows the checkout to feature/textstats before the plan commit), so no worktree or branch question came up.

observations.description: The log has 13 compaction-boundary pairs between 21:24 and 21:38, roughly one per minute. After every compaction the controller re-reads SKILL.md, the prompt templates and the ledger (progress.md). The loop stayed correct, but this cost a lot of time and tokens. The small autoCompactWindow (100000) in the fixture likely causes this, but the re-reads after each compaction add to it.

Wrong co-author trailer on one commit: the agent itself said 301ec27 (wordCount) reads 'Claude Sonnet 5.5' while the others say Opus. It had also amended Task 2 for the same problem (reflog: cd065cd → 507a3cf via 'commit (amend)'). It caught the Task 1 case only at the end and did not fix it.

Before Task 1, the agent stopped to ask a multiple-choice question about test gaps in the plan (unused PASSAGE constants, missing tests). I answered 'Proceed as you recommend.' using the 'Type something' option. It then added tests beyond the plan's counts: 70 total instead of the plan's 32.

The screen showed '(another command ran in this repository at the same time; a change made by either may show under either result)' while the Task 3 implementer ran in the background and the controller ran shell commands. This could confuse users, and it hints at the controller and implementer touching the repo at the same time.

Startup dialogs: the trust-folder and bypass-permissions prompts both default to 'No, exit'. A 'Newer Opus model available: Currently pinned Opus 5' prompt appeared even though the session was launched with --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No.
Codex is not installed, so the optional Codex reviews were skipped. The agent said each skip was logged for a later sweep.

criteria.criterion: All four functions are exported from src/textstats.js with test files, committed, and npm test passes
criteria.evidence: src/textstats.js:141 `module.exports = { wordCount, sentenceCount, topWords, readingTimeMinutes };`. test/ contains wordCount, sentenceCount, topWords and readingTimeMinutes .test.js. git log shows 301ec27 wordCount, 507a3cf sentenceCount, c3e50cd topWords, 875661b readingTimeMinutes. npm test: `tests 70 … pass 70 fail 0`. git status is clean.

criteria.criterion: Each task is reviewed before the next task starts
criteria.evidence: Dispatch order from the session log: Implement T1 21:24:12 → Review T1 21:25:30, which ended 21:25:42 → Implement T2 21:27:19 → Review T2 21:29:20, ended 21:29:34 → Implement T3 21:30:23 → Review T3 21:32:59, ended 21:33:13 → Implement T4 21:34:38 → Review T4 21:36:33, ended 21:36:48. Every review returned '✅ Spec compliant' before the next implementer was dispatched.

criteria.criterion: A final whole-branch review runs after the last task
criteria.evidence: Agent 'Final whole-branch code review' (Opus 5.5) was dispatched at 21:38:13, after the Task 4 review. Its final message: 'I found no Critical or Important issues. The branch is ready to merge.'

criteria.criterion: The session ends in the finishing step
criteria.evidence: Log shows Skill: hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch. The screen showed the options '1. Merge back to main locally 2. Push and create a Pull Request 3. Keep the branch as-is'. I replied 'Keep the branch as-is' and the agent answered 'I've left feature/textstats as it is… Nothing was merged or pushed'.
